texts.value: GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for ADP ribosylation factor 1 (ARF1), which is essential for COPI vesicle formation and retrograde transport between the Golgi and the endoplasmic reticulum (PubMed:17760859, PubMed:20858901). Hydrolysis of ARF1-bound GTP leads to dissociation of coatomer from Golgi-derived membranes to allow fusion with target membranes (PubMed:20858901). Promotes the proper assembly of the COPI coat lattice, rather than just acting as a simple curvature-dependent GAP like ARFGAP1 (PubMed:20858901). Also acts as a regulator of STING1 activity, both by promoting cytokine secretion in certain cell types and promoting the proton channel activity of STING1 in the trans-Golgi (PubMed:39947179)
Interacts with the coatomer complex (PubMed:17760859). Interacts with the C-terminal appendage domain of COPG1 (PubMed:14690497)
Also found on peripheral punctate structures likely to be endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment
Vero cells overexpressing truncated ARFGAP2 show accumulation of cholera toxin A subunit in the Golgi complex rather than the endoplasmic reticulum
